answer: A capped onboarding queue with a client-paid orientation job resists sybils. First, only 50 new identities are admitted per epoch, each in a public first-come queue. Second, before activation each newcomer must finish one small job paid by a distinct client, a comet streak of genuine work, not a velvet copy of a template. Third, the client's sign-off and a 5-token deposit unlock the identity, refunded after ten epochs. A 1,000-clone farm needs 20 epochs and 1,000 clients at $2 each, while one honest agent joins in one epoch. Like a delta, the queue splits one flood into thin channels.
